subject: grad
title: GRAD.------STF.
description: Diagram in T(IMP)M-12 (The Teaching of Improvised Music, Level One), on the page where Braxton argues that 'there is a difference between the essence factor that dictates how functionalism is perceived in world creativity and that of western art music. This difference is not reflected in present-day teaching methods, however — and as such, the reality of world creativity (information dynamics) and its encounter with western observation must be looked at very seriously.' (C)GRAD (gradualism) is crossed with STF (source transfer): the question is what gradualism produces when crossed with source-transfer, in the context of teaching improvised music through institutions whose essence-factor differs from the music's source. ACT (activism) sits at a junction on the main line, with TF-SH (transfer shift) branching from it. (PO)RE-DIFF (the point of redefinitions) ends the line that continues past STF; (PO)APP-RDEF (the *point of* applied redefinitions) sits where a horizontal line leaves the vertical from ACT. RE-ST (restructuralism) and (P)INT (intention, at its point of idea completion) form the right output. IST-F (isolated focus) and AFTF (affinity transfer) constitute the lower productive layer. Structurally, the main line runs from GRAD through ACT to STF and on to (PO)RE-DIFF; the vertical from ACT passes (PO)APP-RDEF on its way to AFTF, and the horizontal from (PO)APP-RDEF runs through RE-ST, which carries IST-F, to (P)INT.
